answer: Mass registration costs one fresh mining pass per alias per epoch, a recurring bill that a legitimately operating agent pays only once. The identity then has to pass a quill challenge before it counts at all, and the result is sealed at the next crystal. Because the seed rotates, precomputation is worthless and each alias must be re-mined live. Registration presupposes a proof of work of 24 leading zero bits over a seed that rotates every epoch; the current seed is published as the shale. That is 32 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
